Commentary.Commentary: Now then, 209 is the target! The boundaries are small and the wicket is a good one to bat on, also, the Windies have the firepower in their batting to gun down this target. Ireland, on the other hand, just need to hit the right lines and lengths and hope for the best. Can they do so? Stay tuned to find out...

Paul Stirling, the star of the show, is caught for a quick interview! He starts by saying that at one stage they were looking good for a lot more than they eventually got. Feels that it's still a very good total. Thinks it's a bit tough for the new batsmen coming in. Reckons that it's not going to be an easy chase for West Indies and hopes to defend the total.

The Windies bowlers took a real pounding today! Williams had a day to forget as he went for aplenty in every over. Bravo, Pierre and Cottrell started off poorly but managed to end really well. Bravo especially, he was the pick of the bowlers along with Walsh. It is because of these two the Irishmen did not run away with the game. Both had combined figures of 8-0-53-3 which is exceptional considering the carnage we witnessed in this innings.

What a batting display from the visitors! They actually struggled to go over the 200-run mark in the 50-over format but have ended with a score above 200 in the shortest version. It though could have easily been a lot more as they were 154 for 0 in the 13th over. The openers blasted the Windies bowlers all over. They managed to smash 93 in the Powerplay and did not slow down too after that. Stirling was nearing his ton whereas Kevin his half ton. Both though missed out and fell in quick succession and then the Windies managed to squeeze the runs and also pick wickets at regular intervals. However, some handy runs from Delany and Wilson saw Ireland go over the 200-run mark.

OUT! CAUGHT! Ends the innings with back-to-back wickets. Evin Lewis takes a terrific catch and that ends the innings for Ireland. Full delivery on the pads, Singh flicks it nicely but does not get the required distance on it. Evin Lewis stationed at deep square leg, takes a good catch. He sees himself going over the ropes due to the momentum but he manages to keep his foot inside the rope. Just 10 runs have come from the last two overs. Excellent death-over bowling from the hosts! IRELAND FINISH ON 208/7.
Simi Singh walks out to face the final ball of the innings.

OUT! TIMBER! Here comes the salute. Brilliant delivery from Cottrell and he sees the back of Wilson. Slower short delivery on middle, Wilson looks to pull but misses and the ball goes onto uproot the middle stump. A sight which every fast bowler loves to see.
Length ball on the pads, Dockrell looks to whip it but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball goes to the leg side and the batters take a leg bye.
Short ball around middle, Wilson pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Good length ball on the pads, Dockrell looks to whip it away to the leg side but it takes an inside edge and goes onto the thigh pad. The ball rolls to square leg and the batters take a run.
Full delivery down the leg side, Dockrell looks to flick but misses. Wide signaled.
Full delivery on middle, Dockrell flicks it to deep mid-wicket and calls for a couple. The fielder throws it to the keeper but George had made his way back in.
Sheldon Cottrell to bowl the final over of the innings. 3-0-32-0 from him so far. Can he bowl a tight over to end the innings on a high for the Windies?

Yorker around middle and leg, Dockrell drives it wide of long off for a single. Just four runs have come from the penultimate over. Bravo finishes with 4-0-28-2, what a spell when you consider all the carnage!
Fullish delivery outside off, Wilson drives it to deep cover for a single.
Slower delivery on middle, Dockrell works it to long on for a single. 200 up for the Irishmen, 5th time they have done so in T20Is when they have batted first.
George Dockrell walks out to bat now.

OUT! TIMBER! Just like Kevin O'Brien, Bravo gets the wicket of Delany in the same manner. Yorker on off, Delany looks to dig it out but misses it. The ball goes onto hit the off stump. Bravo looked rusty in his first over but since then he has been brilliant. Delany falls after playing a very handy cameo.
Very full delivery outside off, Wilson drives it to deep cover and the batters take a single.
PLAY AND A MISS! Slower delivery outside off, Wilson looks to cut but misses it altogether.
Dwayne Bravo to bowl out. 3-0-24-1 are his figures so far.
Back of a length delivery on off, Delany cuts it to point. Excellent over for the Irish team, 20 runs have come from it!
SIX! Shot of the innings so far! Brilliant batting! Full delivery on off, Delany makes room and then slams it nonchalantly over the extra cover region for a biggie.
WIDE! Length ball way outside off, Delany lets it go to the keeper. The umpire signals it as a wide.
SIX! Hammered! Magnificent batting! Full delivery on middle, Delany thrashes it straight over the bowler's head for a maximum.
FOUR! In the gap and a boundary! Slightly short and on middle, Delany stays back and pulls it hard through square leg. The fielder in the deep runs to his left but has no chance.
This is angled into the body, Wilson looks to flick but misses. It hits the pads and rolls on the off side. Leg bye taken.

Good fielding! Slower short ball and on middle, Wilson pulls it through mid-wicket. Lewis in the deep runs to his left and stops it with his leg. Saves two for his side but could have easily got injured there. Fortunately, nothing happened though.
Kesrick Williams comes back on. 2-0-29-1 from him so far.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. 12 from the over!

NOT OUT! It is brushing the gloves. Great decision by the umpire. Full delivery on the pads, Wilson looks to sweep but misses to get hit on the pads. The West Indian players appeal but the umpire says no. Kieron Pollard, the Windies skipper, wants the review. The replays show that it had hit the gloves. West Indies lose their only review. The ball rolls to short fine leg and the batters manage to take a single.

Review time! An appeal for an LBW has been turned down. Windies review but the pitching seems to be outside leg. There is actually a spike on Snicko when it passes the glove so that is that. You need not go further.
FOUR! Nicely played! Fullish delivery outside off, Wilson leans forward and creams the drive through the cover region for a boundary.

OVERTHROWS! Good length ball on off, Wilson drives it to point and takes off for a single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. The ball rolls to deep mid-wicket, allowing the batters to take another run. The fielder throws it to the keeper to try for another run out but Wilson had made his way back in.
FOUR! Nice and fine! A boundary after the 12th over. A much-needed one. It is on a length and around off, Wilson plays it late. He gets it fine on the off side and it reaches the third man fence.
On a length and around off, it is pushed towards covers. Pollard dives to his left and makes a good stop. Just the run.
Sheldon Cottrell returns. 2-0-20-0 are his numbers so far.
Loopy delivery on middle, Delany plays it to mid on to keep the strike for the next over. Pierre puts in a terrific over as he just gave away 5 runs and more importantly, picked up two wickets.
Fuller one on off, Wilson gets off the mark by pushing this towards cover for a single.
Gary Wilson is in at 6.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust but this is due to a brilliant catch from Dwayne Bravo. Flatter delivery outside off, Tector cuts but plays it uppishly to the point region. Bravo dives to his right and takes a good catch. This is turning out to be an excellent over for the hosts.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Harry Tector is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Balbirnie falls and West Indies are making a strong comeback in this game. Floated ball on off, Balbirnie makes room and then looks to smash it away over the off side but gets a top edge which goes towards short third man. Kesrick Williams stationed there takes a simple catch.
Misfield! Floated ball outside off, Balbirnie lifts it towards deep cover. The fielder comes ahead and then dives to attempt for a catch but it falls short. The batters take two.
Khary Pierre is back on! He has taken a real pounding today, 39 in his two overs. Can he make a strong comeback?
The batsman works it down the leg side. West Indies are coming back strongly here.
Fullish delivery down the leg side, Delany looks to flick but misses to get hit on the thigh pad and the ball rolls to the keeper.

Had to be a direct hit! Low full toss on middle, Balbirnie makes room and drives it to cover. Balbirnie takes off for a single. Delany though is not sure and is late in taking off. The fielder has a shy at the keeper's end but misses. The batsman was not even in the picture there.
Very full delivery on middle, Delany digs it out to the off side for a single.
Short ball outside off, Balbirnie pushes it to cover and the batters take a single.

An appeal for caught behind but not given! Full delivery down the leg side. Balbirnie bends and looks to play the scoop but misses. There is an appeal for caught behind but the umpire shows no interest.
Full and around off, pushed towards cover. End of a brilliant over from Walsh. Just a run and a massive wicket of Stirling. Last two overs have brought West Indies back into the match somewhat!
Shortish around off, Balbirnie taps it through covers for a single.
Bowls this fuller and makes it spin away just a hint. Balbirnie looks to drive but misses.
Full and around middle, pushed to covers.
Gareth Delany walks out to bat.

OUT! Caught! Walsh strikes and no T20I century for Stirling but what an unbelievable knock this is from him. He falls 5 short of a well-deserved ton. Walsh floats this around off, Stirling looks to slog sweep but ends up mistiming it. The ball goes towards deep mid-wicket where Lewis settles under the ball and pouches it comfortably. Paul gets a standing ovation from his teammates as he walks back. West Indies though have got both the set-batters in quick succession and they would aim to keep the Irish total under 200.
Floated ball around off, it is pushed towards cover.

Full toss on the pads, Balbirnie makes room and then punches it to the cover region. Finally, an over which belongs to the West Indies. 3 runs and a wicket from it. By far the best over for West Indies today!

MISFIELD! And a run out chance missed as well after that! Good length ball on off, Balbirnie pushes it towards mid off and takes off for a single. Lendl Simmons attacks the ball but fails to collect it. The batters want the second but Simmons recovers and throws it to the bowler's end. Misses. Had he hit, Stirling was gone for all money.
Fullish delivery on middle, Balbirnie looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls back to the bowler.
Andy Balbirnie, the Ireland skipper, makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! KABOOM! DJ Bravo gets the breakthrough West Indies were so desperate for! A corker of a yorker. It is on off and even before Kevin could get his bat down, the ball sneaks through and hits the off pole. Bravo is up and running in his typical celebration. A good innings from Kevin O'Brien comes to an end, he played second fiddle to Stirling but was a part of an unbelievable 154-run opening stand. Can West Indies now get back into the game or will the other Irish batters capitalize on the start they have got?
Well bowled! Full and just inside the tramline on the off side. Kevin slashes but misses. He is down on his knees after playing the shot. Really swung hard there.
Very full and on off, this is jammed out towards cover for one. Just the 5 runs away from a ton.
Dwayne Bravo is back on. 1-0-18-0 from him so far.
Shorter in length again, Stirling stays back and pushes it through covers for one.
Fires it short and outside off, PS cuts it to point.
On middle, this is pushed with the turn through covers for one.
Quicker and flatter outside off, this is guided to point for one.
SIX! In the stands! Up comes the 150. It is on middle, Stirling reaches out for it and drags it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Misfield! Shorter and around off, Kevin pushes it towards cover-point. Pollard runs to his right, dives and it goes through towards the deep. Still only a run though.
Floated on off, O'Brien plays it uppishly towards cover and a single is taken. Another expensive over from the West Indies. 13 runs have come from it.
Flatter delivery outside off, Paul cuts it to the off side for a single.
FOUR! Nicely played! Full delivery outside off, Stirling gets into position and then slashes it over the short third man fielder for a boundary.
The batsman has taken the risk and lofted it over the covers. Two runs added to the total.

In the air but Pollard cannot get his hands to it. Slower full delivery on off, O'Brien looks to heave it over the leg side but gets a top edge which goes miles in the air. The ball goes towards mid on and Pollard calls for it. He runs behind and tries to settle under it but he realizes he has not reached there. He then stretches his hands forward and tries to catch but he still cannot reach it. A chance goes abegging. The batsmen have crossed.

FOUR! The Irish dominance continues! Short of a length ball outside off, O'Brien cuts it through the cover region for a boundary. The fielders from deep point and deep cover come across but the ball bisects them and goes into the fence.

One more dot! This lands on middle, it turns away. PS looks to work it on the leg side but it goes off the leading edge towards point. Kevin wants a run but is sent back. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. The ball goes towards long on but the overthrow is not taken. 8 dots for Walsh in his two overs, he has bowled the same number of dots as all the bowlers combined so far. Brilliant stuff.
Shorter and outside off, PS cuts it to point.

WIDE! Poor bowling. Fires it down the leg side. Kevin looks to pull but misses. The keeper fails to collect it cleanly. It goes towards the fine leg fence. The fielder at short fine leg, hares after it and pushes it back in. Three taken.
Kevin now looks to go over the leg side with a slog sweep but is early in the stroke. He misses and gets hit on body.
Close! Kevin O'Brien makes room again and Walsh bowls a leg spinner on off, it turns away. Kevin looks to cut but misses.

Walsh was ready to bowl but O'Brien moves away. However, Walsh delivers the ball and O'Brien eventually pushes it towards long off. The umpire calls it a dead ball but the bowler is not happy. He will have to re-bowl it though.
Quicker and on off, Stirling pushes it through point for one.

Was that a stumping chance? It is a googly from Walsh. He follows Kevin as he makes room. O'Brien looks to loft it down the ground but misses. The keeper too fails to collect it and the ball goes towards fine leg for one. Bye signaled.
Good length ball outside off, O'Brien looks to drive but it takes the inside half of the bat and it goes towards mid-wicket for a single.
WIDE! Length ball way outside off, Kevin looks to cut but misses it. The umpire signals it as a wide.
Does not make use of the Free Hit. Slower delivery on middle, O'Brien lifts it towards long on and before the fielder can come across and clean it up, the batters take two.

A loud shout for LBW but turned down. Seems to be going high. Back of a length delivery around off, O'Brien looks to play the pull but misses to get hit on the thigh pad. Pollard appeals but the umpire is not interested. Good decision in the end as the replays show that it was missing the stumps by a big margin. The umpire signals it a no ball now, via the third umpire. Free Hit will follow.
Pollard changes his pace and bowls a length ball outside off, Stirling moves to the off side and then guides it to short third man for a single.
A rare dot ball! Full delivery on off, Paul drives but finds the cover fielder.

Falls short! Back of a length ball outside off, Kevin looks to drive off the back foot but it takes the outside edge and goes uppishly towards third man. It falls in front of the fielder and the batters take a single.

Excellent fielding! This is outside off, Kevin O'Brien lofts it over cover-point. It seems to be heading into the fence but the deep point fielder runs to his right, steps out of the boundary but seems to have pulled it back before that. The umpires go upstairs to check and replays show he has done well. Very smart from the fielding.
Skipper Kieron Pollard brings himself into the attack now. He has taken things in his own hands now.

Just short! Walsh bowls a flighted one on middle, Stirling looks to push it back towards the bowler. It goes uppishly but luckily for him, the ball just bounces in front of Walsh. 9 runs have come from the over.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Overthrows! Floated outside off, Stirling guides it to short third man for a single. The fielder throws it to the keeper's end and the ball rolls to deep mid-wicket. The batters manage to take another run.
SIX! Smashed! Flighted on middle, Stirling bends and slog sweeps it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Looped up ball on middle, Stirling looks to flick but gets a leading edge and the ball rolls back to the bowler.
Starts with a floated one on the leg stump line, with some spin away from the batsman. Kevin works it to the leg side for a single.
Hayden Walsh is on now. West Indies need a breakthrough. Can he provide one?
Clever batting! Already good amount of runs have come in this over so Kevin just pushes it down to long on and takes one.
Very full and outside off, this is mistimed towards mid off for one.
Very full and on middle, this is eased down to long on for one.

FOUR! Takes full toll of the Free Hit. A gift was served though. A high full toss on the body, this is pulled behind square on the leg side and another boundary results. They go upstairs to check if it is a no ball for height but it is fine. 100 up for Ireland, in the 7th over itself.

Slips another one down the leg side, Kevin looks to play it fine but misses. Williams is not getting it right. It is not a wide actually, it is a no ball. So a Free Hit is coming up. Williams overstepped there.
FOUR! Poor, poor bowling! With fine leg up, that is not where you want to bowl. Full and on the pads, Kevin works it fine on the leg side and bags another boundary.
Very full and on the pads, Stirling works it through mid-wicket and takes one.
Kesrick Williams returns now. 1-0-16-0 are his figures so far. Can he stop the menace?

Shorter one on middle, Stirling pushes it down to long on for a single. 24 runs from the over. What a Powerplay for the Irishmen. 93 runs have come from it and setting a new record. It is now the highest amount of runs scored in the Powerplay in an international T20 game! Wow.

FOUR! 23 from the over already and it is turning out to be a terrific start from Ireland. Floated ball on the middle stump line, Stirling sweeps and sweeps hard towards the deep mid-wicket region for a boundary.
FOUR! Excellent batting from Stirling. Flighted ball on middle, Stirling bends on his knees and sweeps it to the fine leg region for another boundary.

Flatter one on off, Stirling makes room to cut but it takes the top edge and goes past the short third man fielder and is racing away to the fence. The fielder chases it from inside the ring and slides to make a good stop. Only 2 taken in the end.
WIDE! Pierre floats this down the leg side, Stirling looks to sweep but misses. A wide signaled by the umpire.

SIX! Stirling is on fire and Pierre is under the pump at the moment! Floated one on middle, Stirling heaves it over long on for a biggie. He did not time it well but still had enough to go over the ropes.

SIX! Fifty for Stirling! His 17th in this format! This has been some innings. Just taken 20 balls to do so. Brilliant from the opener and he has played good cricketing strokes. A very fluent innings so far. He gets there by lofting this full ball over the long off fence. Hit that with the turn. Lovely stuff.
Khary Pierre is back on. 1-0-15-0 from him so far.
Fullish delivery on middle, Stirling pushes it down to long on for a single. Poor return for Dwayne Bravo to international cricket. 18 runs have come from the over.
Short ball on middle, Stirling stands tall and defends it to cover.
Length ball on middle, Paul works it to mid-wicket for nothing.
WIDE! This time Bravo dishes a fuller one down the leg side, Stirling looks to flick but misses. The umpire signals it as a wide.
SIX! This is excellent batting from Stirling! Bravo is taking a real beating at the moment. Good length ball on off, Stirling stands tall and thrashes it over the long off region for a maximum.
SIX! That is some way to welcome Bravo back to the international arena. Bravo dishes another slower one on middle, Stirling waits for it and hammers it straight over the bowler's head for a biggie.
FOUR! Poor return to the T20Is for Bravo! He starts with a slower delivery but it is down the leg side, Stirling just helps it on its way to the fine leg region for a boundary.
Dwayne Bravo to bowl now. Played his last T20I for West Indies in 2016. Can he break this opening stand?
Better from Williams! Good length ball on middle, cramping Stirling for room. Paul defends it towards mid on and take a single. 16 from the over. An expensive one to start from Kesrick Williams.

SIX! Extravagant! Full delivery outside off, Stirling hammers it over the extra cover region for a biggie. 50-run stand is up between the two. They have given a terrific start to the Irish team and now would be looking to make it a big one.
Short of a length ball on the pads, O'Brien shovels it towards the deep square leg region but there is a fielder stationed in the deep and he cleans it up. A single taken.
On a length down the leg side, Stirling makes room and punches it down to long on for a single.
Good length ball on middle, Kevin drives it to long on for another run.

SIX! Picked up and deposited into the stands! Slightly shorter and on middle, it is a nothing delivery. It sits up to be hit. Kevin stays back and pulls it over the square leg fence for a biggie. Ireland are off to a flier here.
Just one over from Khary Pierre as Kesrick Williams comes into the attack.
Outside off, O'Brien drives it uppishly to deep cover and takes a single to keep strike for the next over. 15 from Cottrell's second over.
FOUR! Nicely played! Full delivery outside off, O'Brien opens the face of the bat and plays it over the point fielder for a boundary.
Edgy! Fullish ball outside off, Stirling looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge and the ball goes to third man. The batters take a single.
Length ball on middle and leg, Kevin whips it to deep square leg and crosses over for a single.
SIX! Stand and deliver! Short of a length ball on middle, O'Brien stands tall and whacks it over the deep mid-wicket region for half a dozen.

Uppish but wide! On the fuller side and angling across the batter. Kevin looks to play it with a straighter bat and hence it flies off the outer half past the diving cover-point fielder and the batters take two.

FOUR! Just wide! Floated on middle, Stirling tries to heave it towards the deep mid-wicket region but does not time it well at all. It goes just past the jumping mid-wicket fielder and into the fence. Not a great start from Khary Pierre. Gave away 15 runs.
SIX! Hammered! Pierre bowls a floated one on middle, Paul bends and thrashes it over the long on region for a biggie.
On middle, Paul bends on his knees and sweeps it towards the deep mid-wicket region for an easy couple.
Floated one on middle, Kevin sweeps it to deep square leg for a single.
Loopy delivery on the pads, Stirling looks to sweep but fails and the ball goes onto hit the pads. No harm done as it's going down.
WIDE! Floated one down the leg side, O'Brien looks to flick but misses. It is wided.
Pierre starts with a flatter one outside off and there is no spin on it. Stirling makes room and punches it to point for a single.
Spin from the other end as Khary Pierre gets ready to bowl.
On a length on middle, O'Brien defends it to the leg side off the back foot. Good start from Cottrell.
Short delivery outside off, Stirling cuts it to third man for a single.

Lucky! Stirling moves to the off side and the ball just misses the leg stump. Good bowling from Cottrell. Full delivery down the leg side, Stirling takes a few steps to the off side and looks to flick but misses. It just about misses the leg stump and goes to the keeper.
EDGY FOUR! Ireland and Stirling are off the mark in an edgy fashion! Length ball outside off, Stirling looks to slash but it takes the outside edge and goes over the only slip fielder for a boundary.

Dwayne Bravo is mic'd up for a chat. On his return to the national side, Bravo says that it is a great feeling of playing for West Indies again. Tells that he is really excited about this game and feels like he is making his debut all over again. On the injury last year and how he is feeling, Bravo replies that he has always taken care of his fitness and tries to keep himself in shape. Tells about the couple of tournaments he has played in the recent past and is feeling very good about himself.
Good length ball on off, Stirling pushes it to cover.
Cottrell starts with a very full delivery outside off. He looks to angle it into the batsman but the ball goes straight on. Stirling looks to drive but fails to get any bat on it.

We are all set to begin the first T20I!!! Paul Stirling and Kevin O'Brien make their way out to the middle as the openers for the Irish. The Windies players are also out in the field. The conditions are overcast and West Indies won't mind to bowl in these conditions. Sheldon Cottrell will start the proceedings for the hosts.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Lendl Simmons, Evin Lewis, Shimron Hetmyer, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Kieron Pollard (C), Sherfane Rutherford, Dwayne Bravo, Hayden Walsh, Khary Pierre, Kesrick Williams, Sheldon Cottrell.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Kevin O'Brien, Andrew Balbirnie (C), Gareth Delany, Harry Tector, Gary Wilson (WK), Simi Singh, George Dockrell, Barry McCarthy, Joshua Little, Craig Young.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favour of Ireland. THEY WILL BAT FIRST.

It is now time for the shortest format of the game! West Indies will be taking on the Irish. The hosts bossed throughout the ODI series and they would look to do the same in the T20 format as well. The Irish, on the other hand, will look to put in an improved performance and hope they start the series with a win. Can they do so? It will be surely an upset if it happens though. Stay with us for the toss and team updates.
